cards.headline: Oil patches spotted in S’pore’s southern waters off Pulau Sebarok, Pulau Semakau and Selat Pauh: MPA
bullets: Oil patches were seen in Singapore's southern waters near Pulau Sebarok and Pulau Semakau.
The Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) is investigating the source of the oil.
MPA has activated oil spill response teams and alerted nearby terminals.
No impact on ship traffic or port operations has been reported.
Authorities are taking steps to protect shorelines from the oil.

cards.headline: Heavy traffic expected at Woodlands, Tuas checkpoints during Deepavali long weekend
bullets: Expect heavy traffic at Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints from Nov 6 to Nov 9.
This is due to the Deepavali long weekend and increased security checks.
Travellers are advised to plan journeys and travel during off-peak hours.
Check traffic conditions before you go and use the MyICA app for faster clearance.

cards.headline: Educate first for more constructive outcomes, says Foo Cexiang of his push for citizen participation
bullets: Minister Foo Cexiang believes educating citizens first helps them join policy talks constructively.
He wants to create platforms for passionate Singaporeans to contribute and thrive.
Foo has led pilot projects like a recycling trial and participatory budgeting in his ward.
He sees citizen engagement as key to shaping communities and neighbourhoods.
His new roles involve significant communication and travel, which he explains to his young daughters.

cards.headline: New MOS Foo Cexiang wants to help workers switch sectors, find jobs more quickly for those who reskill
bullets: Minister Foo Cexiang wants to help retrenched workers switch jobs and find new roles.
He aims to improve support for people who reskill but still struggle to find suitable jobs.
The government will study why some job seekers get stuck and design solutions.
Companies and society must support workers changing careers, especially older ones.
MOM is also looking into 'fractional work' for experienced seniors.

cards.headline: At least 20 S’pore schools hire external manpower to help with student discipline and management
bullets: At least 20 schools are hiring outsiders to help manage student discipline and behaviour.
These hired officers will handle tasks like conflict resolution and talking to parents.
The move aims to reduce teachers' workload and allow them to focus on teaching.
Some schools prefer officers with experience in police or military service.
New online tools will also be introduced by 2027 for students to report issues.

cards.headline: Oil patches spotted in Singapore's southern waters; source under investigation: MPA
bullets: Oil patches were found in Singapore's southern waters near Pulau Sebarok and Pulau Semakau.
Authorities are investigating the source of the oil patches spotted in the sea.
No oil was seen near popular areas like Sentosa or the East Coast.
Port operations and ship traffic have not been affected by the oil patches.
Clean-up efforts are underway to remove the oil from the water.

cards.headline: Heavy traffic expected at Singapore-Malaysia land checkpoints during Deepavali long weekend
bullets: Expect heavy traffic at Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints from Nov 6 to Nov 9.
ICA advises planning trips and travelling during off-peak hours.
Security checks are stepped up due to global security concerns.
Use the MyICA app with QR codes for faster immigration clearance.
More than 6.1 million travellers used checkpoints during September holidays.

cards.headline: Over 1,300 BTO flats with shorter waiting time of under 3 years to be offered in Sembawang in November
bullets: November BTO sales will offer 1,310 flats in Sembawang with waiting times under three years.
Other BTO projects in Bayshore and Tengah will also have waiting times of just over three years.
These shorter waiting time flats aim to help more Singaporeans get their new homes sooner.
The Sembawang project includes shops, a preschool, and is near a new park and community hub.

cards.headline: Police to use single caller ID 6000 0999 from Nov 2 to combat impersonation scams
bullets: Police calls will now use a single number, 6000 0999, from November 2.
This new number will help people spot real police calls and avoid scams.
Calls from this number will be followed by a text from 'gov.sg'.
Scammers impersonating officials cost victims over S$142 million this year.
Police were the most impersonated agency, with S$53.3 million lost.

cards.headline: AI can make art in seconds – how are artists in Singapore fighting to keep their craft alive?
bullets: Some artists say AI art tools steal their work without permission.
Artists are worried AI might reduce the value of human creativity.
Singaporean artists are finding ways to protect their work from AI.
Some designers use AI for ideas but avoid using it for final products.

cards.headline: After Louvre heist and string of thefts, Europe’s smaller museums are on guard
bullets: Artworks by Cézanne, Renoir, and Matisse worth millions were stolen from an Italian museum.
Thieves are increasingly targeting smaller European museums after a major Louvre heist.
Many smaller museums lack basic security like cameras or emergency plans.
France is giving 30 million euros to help smaller museums improve security.

cards.headline: Asset light or asset heavy? It need not be ‘either or’, says GuocoLand CEO
bullets: GuocoLand CEO says property firms don't have to be strictly asset-light or asset-heavy.
The company is open to selling assets if there are good chances to reinvest the money.
GuocoLand does not keep properties just for the sake of owning them.

cards.headline: 2027 BMW 3 Series review: Petrol still beats electric, but it’s close
bullets: The new petrol BMW M350 is faster than its electric i3 50 version.
The petrol M350 is lighter by about 345kg, making it more agile.
The electric i3 50 can travel up to 912km on a single charge.
Both cars share the same modern interior design and large touchscreen.
Some electric car issues like the glass roof without a shade remain.

cards.headline: 2026 BMW i3 review: The EV that could shake a petrolhead to the core
bullets: The new electric BMW i3 will debut in January 2027 with 469 horsepower.
It can charge 423 km of range in just 10 minutes with a 400 kW charger.
The i3 boasts a 912 km range and accelerates from 0-100 kmh in 4.7 seconds.
Despite its performance, the electric i3 may lack the emotional thrill of a petrol engine.
The car features a panoramic display and a large touchscreen, but has limited rear passenger space.

cards.headline: Fundraiser set up for Tampines Ave 12 fatal crash victims' 6-year-old son
bullets: A fundraiser has raised over S$8,600 for the 6-year-old son of a couple who died in a Tampines crash.
The couple, both 24, died on Oct. 29 after a car hit their motorcycle.
A 30-year-old man faces charges for dangerous driving causing death.
The boy is now staying with his late mother's family.

cards.headline: Chris Hemsworth dines at Nong Geng Ji at Jewel Changi Airport, manager requests photo
bullets: Hollywood star Chris Hemsworth ate at Nong Geng Ji restaurant in Jewel Changi Airport.
He was there with his three children before dinner time on Sunday.
Restaurant staff recognised him and asked for a photo, which he agreed to.
Hemsworth was in Singapore after filming in Thailand.

cards.headline: Thin boy in China with poor appetite assumed ill, but devours KFC meal, doctor finds out home-cooked food not tasty
bullets: A thin boy in China who refused to eat was given KFC by a doctor.
The boy ate the fast food eagerly, suggesting he disliked home-cooked meals.
Doctors advised parents not to force picky eaters and consider their food preferences.
Adults and children can have different tastes, so meals might need changing.

cards.headline: Jewel Changi Airport Guide: 23 Things To Do The Next Time You Have A Layover At The World’s Best Airport
bullets: Jewel Changi Airport features the world's tallest indoor waterfall, the Rain Vortex, which is 40m high.
You can watch a light and sound show at the Rain Vortex every night.
The Forest Valley has many plants and walking paths, offering a cool indoor nature experience.
Canopy Park on the top floor has attractions like mazes and thrilling slides for all ages.
There are also themed gardens and animal topiary sculptures made of flowers.

cards.headline: We Got To Ride Sentosa’s Self-Driving Shuttle Service Before It Launches In 2027 & Here’s What It’s Like
bullets: Sentosa will launch a free self-driving shuttle service in early 2027.
The electric shuttles use sensors and cameras to navigate the island.
Rides can be booked via the TADA app, with a safety operator onboard during trials.
The first phase covers western Sentosa with 21 pick-up and drop-off points.
The shuttle stops cautiously for pedestrians and brakes smoothly.

cards.headline: You Can Kayak Through Punggol On A Guided Tour To Explore The Waterways & Spot Wildlife
bullets: You can now kayak on a guided 5km to 6km tour through Punggol Waterway.
The tour uses special kayaks pedalled by your feet, freeing your hands for photos.
Spot wildlife like otters, monitor lizards, and over 100 bird species.
Beginners are welcome, with instructors guiding you and providing safety gear.
Sessions last two hours and cost from $49.90 per person.
